source.title: Concept-Monitor: Understanding DNN training through individual neurons
source.authors: Mohammad Ali Khan; Tuomas P. Oikarinen; T. Weng

page_placements.theme: Training regime, data, objective and architecture shift unit-level concept alignment in vision, audio and genomic models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies concept descriptions of neurons in vision networks during training, but does not test the claim versions about pole-level jobs, language models, held-out explanation validation, or attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-interpretability measurements in ResNet vision models, including a concept-diversity regularizer comparison. These are related findings, but they do not measure the claim's pole-level job shares or validate explanations on held-out activations. No results are recorded for the claim versions; the regularizer counts are retained as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper takes for granted that single vision neurons (ResNet-18/34/50) have one describable concept. It labels each neuron's best concept with CLIP-Dissect and counts a neuron as interpretable when its similarity score passes a tunable threshold. It then reports its own monitoring method and regularizer results. It never checks whether neurons have one main job, two jobs or none (V1, V2), and never tests InceptionV1 polysemantic examples (V3). It builds no neuron attribution graphs (V5) and does not test explanations on held-out activations (V6, V7). Its interpretable-neuron counts under a regularizer, pruning and adversarial training touch V4's 'regularization' clause only loosely. The count is a detector-threshold artefact, not a share of explained neurons, and nothing is compared across tool quality or architecture generation. So these results go under fits_no_version, not V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors present Concept-Monitor as an automatic way to track neuron concepts during vision-network training. They say the concept-diversity regularizer improved accuracy and concept diversity. Interpretable-neuron count rose only for Res18; Table 1 shows it fell for Res50, and the authors do not discuss that drop.
record.recipe_differences: Uses concept detectors and a similarity threshold to describe neurons in vision networks; it does not assign pole-level jobs or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported number of interpretable neurons depends on the concept-detector similarity threshold; the paper notes that increasing the threshold decreases the count.

fits_no_version.finding: A concept-diversity regularizer raised the interpretable-neuron count in Res18 (106.33 to 147.7) but lowered it in Res50 (544.4 to 361), both on Places365.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training regularizers can shift the number of vision neurons passing a concept-detector threshold, and the direction depends on the model.

fits_no_version.finding: Under iterative magnitude pruning with rewinding to initialization, the fraction of interpretable layer-4 neurons in ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 rose across pruning stages (Fig 4, no numbers given).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zeroing weights alone can make some neurons pass a concept-detector interpretability threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: An adversarially trained ResNet-18 had 30 colour neurons versus 2 in the standard model, and fewer object, scene and part neurons (Fig 6-7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training paradigm changes which concept categories interpretable neurons detect.

record.problems: The study does not test the claim versions. Its neuron interpretations depend on concept sets, detectors, and a similarity threshold; it does not validate the descriptions against held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported concept-tracking observations and metrics were left out because they concern training dynamics, concept categories, or anchor distance rather than the claim's pole-level job shares or held-out explanation tests.

record.verdict_notes: Interpretable-neuron counts depend on the threshold τ: per Appendix C.2, raising τ lowers the count and can remove all interpretable neurons in some layers. Fig 12's caption briefly mentions polysemantic neurons but makes no measurement of them. The original record's T6/discusses was changed to T4/uses_without_test, because the paper relies on neuron-level concept labels as its tool.

rows.subject: Res18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the concept-diversity regularizer and compared with standard training.
rows.note: The paper defines interpretability using a concept-detector similarity threshold; this is not a share of poles with validated single jobs.
rows.check: Values match Table 1. This is a count of neurons whose CLIP-Dissect score passes a threshold, not a share of neurons with a validated single job. The regularizer is the authors' own method, compared against standard training.

rows.subject: Res50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the concept-diversity regularizer and compared with standard training.
rows.note: The paper defines interpretability using a concept-detector similarity threshold; this is not a share of poles with validated single jobs.
rows.check: Values match Table 1 (544.4 to 361, a decrease). Same measure caveat as r1. The authors' text claims interpretability gains only for Res18, not Res50.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: It uses neuron concept labels as a tool without testing the claim. The reader's earlier call (discusses/T6) is also defensible.

tranche.reason: The paper introduces its own monitoring method and regularizer and uses CLIP-Dissect concept labels as a tool. It does not test whether neurons already have clean single jobs.

source_check.notes: Table 1: the interpretable-neuron count fell for Res50 (544.4 to 361), but the text claims a gain only in general terms and mentions only Res18. The count depends on a tunable CLIP-Dissect threshold tau (App. C.2), and the paper does not say what the ± values mean or how many runs were done. Training used Places minibatches as Dprobe; Table 1 used Broden. The Fig 12 caption mentions polysemantic neurons, so 'one concept per neuron' is the method's labelling choice, not a claim the authors make.
